Execute via full TDD cycle (red -> green -> commit). High-severity finding from an adversarial review: reasoning tokens are tracked but structurally can never be priced. No plan@1/spec_file_path exists, proceed directly from this brief -- the design is already worked out from reading the real code, follow it.

Workspace: /Users/gabe/Projects/lumen. Baseline: 11 fixes landed (cb29996..3a374cf), `cargo test --workspace` green.

## The bug

`TokenRateKind` (crates/lumen-model/src/pricing.rs) has exactly four variants -- Input, CacheWrite, CacheRead, Output -- no Reasoning. `TurnTokenUsage` (crates/lumen-model/src/turn.rs) has no `reasoning_tokens` field at all. Codex's adapter (crates/lumen-session/src/adapters/codex.rs) parses a real `reasoning_output_tokens` value from the payload, but since `TurnPricingInput`/`TurnTokenUsage` can't carry it, it's set on the returned `TokenEconomics` struct AFTER `TokenEconomics::calculate` has already summed `total_cost_usd`:
```rust
let mut economics = TokenEconomics::calculate(&[pricing_input], &model_family, &PricingTable::seed(), None);
economics.reasoning_output_tokens = reasoning_output_tokens; // reaches the struct, never reaches the pricing math
```
`TokenEconomics::calculate` itself (crates/lumen-model/src/economics.rs) also hardcodes `reasoning_output_tokens: 0` in the struct it builds internally, before any caller overwrites it. This isn't fixable at one call site -- no adapter, ever, can price reasoning tokens under the current type shape.

## The fix (design already worked out, execute this exactly)

1. Add `Reasoning` as a fifth variant to `TokenRateKind` in crates/lumen-model/src/pricing.rs.

2. Add `pub reasoning_tokens: u64` to `TurnTokenUsage` in crates/lumen-model/src/turn.rs (it already derives `Default`, so `..Default::default()` remains available at any construction site that wants it, but check whether any real construction site currently uses that spread or builds full literals -- see step 5).

3. In `PricingTable::seed()` (crates/lumen-model/src/pricing.rs), add a `TokenRateKind::Reasoning` row for every model that already has an Output row, using THE SAME rate as that model's Output rate. This reflects real, publicly documented billing policy: OpenAI's reasoning-capable models bill reasoning tokens as part of completion/output tokens at the standard output rate (this is genuine, published pricing behavior, not a fabricated number) -- and no provider in this table publishes a DIFFERENT, separate reasoning-token rate, so "same as Output" is the closest defensible default rather than 0.0 (which would silently under-price every reasoning-heavy session) or an invented distinct number. Add a code comment explaining this reasoning explicitly so a future reader understands it's a judgment call, not verified per-model data. If you judge a different, better-justified approach after your own research, you may deviate -- but document your reasoning either way.

4. In `TokenEconomics::calculate` (crates/lumen-model/src/economics.rs):
   - Add `let mut reasoning_tokens_total = 0u64;` alongside the other running totals.
   - Inside the per-turn loop, look up `let reasoning_rate = pricing.rate_for(model_name, tier, TokenRateKind::Reasoning, turn.timestamp);` and add `(usage.reasoning_tokens as f64 / 1_000_000.0) * reasoning_rate` to `turn_cost`. Also add the same term to `turn_baseline_cost` (reasoning tokens should be priced at the SAME rate in both the actual and no-cache-baseline cost, since caching doesn't apply to reasoning tokens -- this keeps `net_savings_usd`/`efficiency_multiplier` internally consistent rather than skewed by reasoning cost appearing in one side but not the other).
   - Accumulate `reasoning_tokens_total += usage.reasoning_tokens;` each turn.
   - Replace the hardcoded `reasoning_output_tokens: 0` in the final `Self { ... }` literal with `reasoning_output_tokens: reasoning_tokens_total`.
   - Also add `reasoning_tokens` to `ModelTokenSummary` if you judge it belongs there for parity with the other four token kinds already tracked per-model (your call -- check whether skipping it leaves an inconsistency worth flagging instead).

5. Fix crates/lumen-session/src/adapters/codex.rs: instead of patching `economics.reasoning_output_tokens` after `calculate()` runs, set `reasoning_tokens: reasoning_output_tokens` directly in the `TurnTokenUsage` literal passed into `TurnPricingInput` (so it flows through the actual pricing math), and remove the now-unnecessary post-hoc `economics.reasoning_output_tokens = reasoning_output_tokens;` line (calculate() will now compute this field correctly itself).

6. **Workspace-wide mechanical migration**: adding a required field to `TurnTokenUsage` will break EVERY existing literal construction site that doesn't use `..Default::default()`. Grep the whole workspace for `TurnTokenUsage {` (crates/lumen-session's four adapters, any test files in crates/lumen-model/tests, crates/lumen-session/tests, crates/lumen-analysis) and add `reasoning_tokens: 0,` (or the real value, for codex.rs per step 5) to each literal construction site that doesn't already spread `..Default::default()`. This is mechanical, not new logic -- do not change any other field's value at these sites.

## TDD steps

1. Write a failing test in crates/lumen-model/tests/test_pricing.rs: build a `TurnPricingInput` with `reasoning_tokens` set to a real non-zero value on a model with a seeded Reasoning rate (e.g. gpt-4o), call `TokenEconomics::calculate`, and assert `total_cost_usd` reflects the reasoning tokens' contribution (compute the expected value by hand: reasoning_tokens/1_000_000 * reasoning_rate, added to the other components) -- NOT just that `reasoning_output_tokens` field is populated (that's necessary but not sufficient; the whole point is the DOLLAR AMOUNT must include it).
2. Confirm red against the current code (should fail to compile initially since `reasoning_tokens` doesn't exist yet, then once the field exists but before the pricing-loop wiring, the cost assertion should fail with a value missing the reasoning contribution).
3. Add a test in crates/lumen-session/tests/test_codex.rs using the real Codex fixture (`real_codex_session_dump`, which already carries a `reasoning_output_tokens` value per TASK-SESSION-004's earlier work) asserting `economics.total_cost_usd` now reflects the fixture's reasoning tokens priced at gpt-4o's rate, not just that `economics.reasoning_output_tokens` is populated as a disconnected field.
4. Implement all fixes (pricing.rs, turn.rs, economics.rs, codex.rs, plus the mechanical migration).
5. Confirm green: new tests pass, full existing test suites for lumen-model and lumen-session pass with no regression (this WILL require updating other pricing/economics tests that assert exact dollar amounts if those tests' fixture models now have a nonzero Reasoning rate contributing when reasoning_tokens happens to be nonzero in their fixtures -- check whether any existing test needs its expected-cost assertion updated because a previously-untracked reasoning contribution is now correctly included; if a test's fixtures never set reasoning_tokens above 0, it's unaffected).
6. Run `cargo test -p lumen-model`, `cargo test -p lumen-session`, then `cargo test --workspace` to confirm zero regressions.
7. Commit.

Report: test results, confirmation of zero regressions, the exact reasoning-rate design decision you made (same-as-output vs. alternative), and the list of files touched by the mechanical TurnTokenUsage migration.

Execute via full TDD cycle (red -> green -> commit). High-severity finding from an adversarial review: token economics is a write-only/read-zero field in the store. No plan@1/spec_file_path exists, proceed directly from this brief -- the design is already worked out from reading the real code.

Workspace: /Users/gabe/Projects/lumen. Baseline: 12 fixes landed (cb29996..b181279), `cargo test --workspace` green.

## The bug

`SessionRepository::upsert_session` (crates/lumen-store/src/repositories/session.rs) never persists `record.economics`'s raw token counts (input_tokens/output_tokens/cache_creation_tokens/cache_read_tokens/per_model) anywhere -- only the derived cost/ratio fields (cache_hit_ratio, total_cost_usd, baseline_cost_usd, net_savings_usd, efficiency_multiplier) get written to the `sessions` table's own columns. `SessionRepository::get_session` correspondingly hardcodes the returned `TokenEconomics`'s token counts and `per_model` map to 0/empty (lines ~148-161) since there's nowhere real to read them from via that code path. `TokenUsageRepository` (crates/lumen-store/src/repositories/token_usage.rs, landed earlier this session) already exists and can INSERT real per-model token_usage rows given a `&TokenEconomics`, but nothing calls it from `upsert_session`, and it has no read method at all (its spec, CRIT-LUMEN-125, only required `insert_token_usage`).

## The fix

1. **Wire `upsert_session` to also persist token usage.** After the existing session-row upsert succeeds, resolve the session's internal integer id (`SELECT id FROM sessions WHERE provider_session_id = ?1`, same pattern used elsewhere in this file and in TokenUsageRepository::resolve_session_id), DELETE any existing `token_usage` rows for that internal id first (`DELETE FROM token_usage WHERE session_id = ?1`) -- this makes repeated `upsert_session` calls for the same session idempotent by fully replacing the per-model breakdown rather than accumulating duplicate rows, since `upsert_session` is explicitly documented (CRIT-LUMEN-033) as callable multiple times for the same (provider, provider_session_id) -- then call `TokenUsageRepository::new(self.conn).insert_token_usage(&record.provider_session_id, &record.economics)` to write the fresh per-model rows. Read TokenUsageRepository's exact current `insert_token_usage` signature/behavior first (crates/lumen-store/src/repositories/token_usage.rs) before wiring this -- do not change that repository's existing insert-only contract, just call it correctly from the new call site.

2. **Add a real read method to TokenUsageRepository** so `get_session` has something real to read from -- there currently is none. Add `pub fn per_model_by_session(&self, session_id: i64) -> Result<std::collections::HashMap<compact_str::CompactString, lumen_model::ModelTokenSummary>, StoreError>` querying `SELECT model_name, input_tokens, cache_write_tokens, cache_read_tokens, output_tokens, cost_usd FROM token_usage WHERE session_id = ?1` and building one `ModelTokenSummary` per row, keyed by model_name. Note: the `token_usage` table has no `turns` column (check `ModelTokenSummary`'s exact fields in crates/lumen-model/src/economics.rs -- it has a `turns: u64` field that `insert_token_usage` never writes anywhere either, since the table schema doesn't have a column for it). Judgment call: either (a) add a new migration (V7, following the exact same append-only pattern RollupRepository's V6 used -- `ALTER TABLE token_usage ADD COLUMN turns INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`, then update both `insert_token_usage` to write it and this new read method to read it, so the round-trip is fully honest, or (b) default `turns: 0` on read and leave a clear code comment flagging the schema gap rather than silently pretending it round-trips.
